detail.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.summary: This revision integrates Renormalization Group (RG) methods and causal graphical frameworks to refine our understanding of memory reliability costs. We find that RG flows suggest universal dissipation bounds are dictated by symmetry-breaking fixed points, while causal graphical hierarchies identify specific edges in the data-generating process where memory must be robust to maintain stability against environment shifts. Furthermore, memory costs in information engines are bounded by the input ensemble's separable-state capacity, extending beyond simple Landauer limits.
detail.reason: Revising the provisional notebook to incorporate new theoretical frameworks regarding universality and causal stability.
